messages.subject: multiplot
parts:
Hi,
I want to change the color of my multipot. The steps I followed are
listed below:


b<-read.csv("Bulle.csv",row.names=1)
mytheme <- theme_bw() +
theme(text = element_text(colour="black"),
axis.title = element_text(size = rel(1.5)))
p1<-ggplot(b,aes(x=Longitude, y=Latitude, size=Diat,colour=Mfluor))+
geom_point(shape=21,colour="black",fill="grey")+
geom_text(aes(y=Latitude+.1,label=CTD),size=4,vjust=1)
p1+mytheme
ss<-p1+mytheme
ss+scale_size_area(max_size=15)
ss+scale_size_area(max_size=10)+scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(0.05,0.35),low="green")

p2<-ggplot(b,aes(x=Longitude, y=Latitude, size=Diat,colour=Mfuco))+
geom_point(shape=21,colour="black",fill="grey")+
geom_text(aes(y=Latitude+.1,label=CTD),size=4,vjust=1)
p2+mytheme
ss<-p2+mytheme
ss+scale_size_area(max_size=15)
ss+scale_size_area(max_size=10)+scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(0.01,0.35),low="green")
multiplot(p1,p2,cols=2)

in my multiplot I get a blue color gradient while I chose the color
green in scale_colour_gradient.

how can I solve this problem?

Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: multiplot
parts:
Can you give a reproducible dataset for which the code applies? 

This is from the docs for ggplot2 at http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3.1/scale_gradient.html ... it should work.

dsub <- subset(diamonds, x > 5 & x < 6 & y > 5 & y < 6)
d <-ggplot(dsub,aes(x, y,colour=z))+geom_point()
d+ scale_colour_gradient(limits=c(3, 4), low="green")
